newsitem.title: UK: IBCA affirms Lucas ratings takes off watch.
newsitem.headline: IBCA affirms Lucas ratings takes off watch.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Thursday it affirmed its BBB plus long-term and A2 short-term ratings for Lucas Industries Plc and removed them from RatingWatch positive.
IBCA said Lucas was placed on RatingWatch with positive implications in May this year when the proposed merger with Varity Corporation of the US was announced. The merger was completed in September.
"The combined LucasVarity is a top ten global automotive component supplier with sales of 4.4 billion stg, of which 66 percent is contributed by Lucas," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA said LucasVarity's particular strength lay in light braking systems, where it was the world number two.

It said the lack of overlap of the two companies' operations in this area provided only limited scope for cost cutting, with Lucas focusing on foundation brakes to the European market and Varity's ABS sold mainly to U.S. vehicle manufacturers.

"Future benefits of the merger will instead rely largely on the degree of success of cross selling. The key opportunity is to market Varity's relatively high-margin ABS to Lucas' substantial European customer base, although such efforts are likely to take some time in producing results," IBCA said.

"The automotive component industry is highly competitive and is characterised by cyclical demand patterns and strong buyer power. Suppliers to vehicle producers are generally forced to reduce prices by 3.0 percent or more in real terms every year," the rating agency said. "Following the merger with Varity, Lucas remains heavily dependent on this industry, which accounts for 75 percent of group sales."

IBCA said the outlook for automotive demand in Europe, although currently healthy, was likely to deteriorate in the near term partly due to budgetary constraints imposed by governments in efforts to fulfil monetary convergence criteria.
"Vehicle sales in the U.S., which have been buoyant for several years, are showing signs of slowing," said IBCA.
